name: What should be included in a remodeling contract before construction starts?

mainEntity.name: What should be included in a remodeling contract before construction starts?
mainEntity.text: What should be included in a remodeling contract before construction starts?

acceptedAnswer.text: A strong remodeling contract should make the project measurable and enforceable. It needs a detailed scope of work, plans or references to the plans, material allowances, payment milestones, and a clear start and completion framework. It should also identify who handles permits, inspections, cleanup, site protection, debris removal, and warranty service. The change-order process should be written clearly so any scope additions are approved before work continues. If the project involves custom finishes, the contract should specify quality standards and what happens if selections are changed after ordering. Homeowners should also verify insurance and licensing documents before signing. In Los Angeles, where remodels can be complex and timelines are sensitive, a vague contract is a major risk. A good contract reduces misunderstandings and helps both sides track progress. If something important is only discussed verbally, it should be added to the written agreement before construction begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: A remodeling contract should include the scope of work, drawings, allowances, payment schedule, start and finish dates, change-order process, warranty terms, and who is responsible for permits and inspections. Missing details usually lead to disputes.
